ops.statement: The Commander plan/survey templates hardcode config_ref: docs/agents/engine-config.json, a path absent in a skill-source (self-hosting) repo. The engine degrades gracefully, but crews rediscover the house inline-config convention every time. Fix candidate: conditionalize the template ref, or note the absent overlay in the handoff/CREW_CONTEXT for skill-source worktrees.
ops.grounding: AGENT_FEEDBACK.md 2026-07-19 cg-fastfollows-198 -- all 4 crews (g1-impl, g1-rev, g2-impl, g2-rev) independently rediscovered inline config over the dead config_ref
ops.bank_reason: Fix is a template/doctrine change needing human authority; re-observe whether it recurs across skill-source runs to decide template-conditionalize vs handoff-note before paying it.

ops.statement: Doc-gate implementer/reviewer handoffs should anchor on section names and code symbols, not absolute line numbers -- line numbers shift as edits land within the same PR and read as stale to the crew.
ops.grounding: AGENT_FEEDBACK.md 2026-07-19 cg-fastfollows-198 -- g2-implementer and g2-reviewer both flagged the 'L205 area' line-number anchor as pre-edit-only
ops.bank_reason: Minor this run; re-observe whether a stale line-number anchor ever causes a real miss (not just a note) before changing handoff-authoring doctrine.

ops.statement: A handoff that dictates a test assertion must ensure it is realizable for the specific type under test. Dictating 'assert the why_ref pointer' on a survey's REFRESH REQUESTED line overreached -- a survey has no why_trail, so the minimal fix renders no why_ref suffix; the crew had to reconcile the spec against the code.
ops.grounding: AGENT_FEEDBACK.md 2026-07-19 cg-fastfollows-198 -- g1-implementer workflow feedback: the #189 test sub-bullet's why_ref-pointer assertion is unrealizable for a survey under the minimal fix
ops.bank_reason: One instance; re-observe whether type-blind test-assertion specs recur enough to warrant a handoff-authoring checklist item vs staying a per-run judgment.
